title: The Histories of Tacitus, with the Bible's world around it
summary: Tacitus's Histories, the Roman historian's account of the civil wars after Nero and the war in Judea, are now in the library in a Conversational English Translation, with study notes on every place the story touches the Bible: Berenice and Agrippa, the governor Felix, the fall of the Temple, and Tacitus's own account of the Jews. Passages a PG-13 film would not show are folded behind a short summary you can open.

items.text: Added Histories of Tacitus: a Conversational English Translation of all 5 books, with 537 study notes and 100 manuscript differences explained, beside the Latin and the Church and Brodribb English.
40 new topic pages, including Alexandria, Antonius Felix, Governor of Judea, The Revolt of the Batavians (AD 69-70), Berenice (Bernice in Acts) and Caesarea (Maritima).
Writings of other peoples can now fold a hard passage behind a short summary. Press Show to read it; the same verse is folded in the Latin and English views too.
